Week of October 12th, 2026. $DELL $XMTR $MPC $TSLA $CON

Last week's list trailed the S&P 500, so here's what we changed plus five names to watch for the rest of the week: two momentum leaders, a refiner repeat, the Tesla buzz and a quiet occupational-health sleeper.

Last week's scorecard (Episode 1, Oct 2 to Oct 9 close)

| Ticker | Reference | Oct 9 close | Return | Note |

|---|---|---|---|---|

| $MPC | $420.15 | $455.03 | +8.3% | Broke its $431 trigger and set a $470 52-week high on Oct 9 |

| $NVDA | $233.95 | $229.28 | -2.0% | Broke its $238 trigger (record close Oct 6), then faded |

| $TWLO | $301.27 | $289.47 | -3.9% | Dipped under the $280 invalidation intraday Oct 12, closed above it |

| $CHEF | $117.94 | $114.32 | -3.1% | Single source for the Oct 9 close |

| $MTRN | $312.16 | $277.11* | -11.2%* | *Oct 8 close; Oct 9 close not confirmed. Below its $285 invalidation |

| Picks average (all 5) | | | about -2.4% | |

| S&P 500 | 7,722.72 | 7,811.54 | +1.15% | |

We trailed the S&P 500 by about 3.5 points, and MPC carried the list. MTRN is counted at its Oct 8 close because its Oct 9 close couldn't be confirmed. What changed: we now cap how far above the 50-day a pick can be, skip stocks right after big no-news pops, skip index-add weeks and earnings weeks, and limit picks per theme.

Market pulse

  • The S&P 500 rose a little over 1% in the week to Oct 9 (+1.15% per Investrade, +1.21% per LPL) and set a record intraday high of 7,844.52.
  • Thursday, Oct 8: a report that OpenAI's revenue was lower than earlier figures hit chip and AI stocks. The Nasdaq fell 1.25%, its worst day since mid-August.
  • The 10-year Treasury yield was near 24-year highs (about 5.24% on Oct 9), and Brent crude stayed above $100.
  • The Russell 2000 was the only major index down on the week (-0.76%, per LPL).
  • Monday, Oct 12: Dow +0.38%, S&P 500 -0.06%, Nasdaq -0.44%. Energy led.
  • Rest of the week: bank earnings, September CPI (Wed), PPI and retail sales (Thu), TSMC earnings (Thu) and a speech by Fed Chair Warsh.
  • Takeaway: gains are narrow, so be picky.

The picks

  • $DELL (momentum): Record AI-server backlog of about $95B and a raised full-year outlook of about $192B. Levels: pivot about $596 (52-week high), support $565, invalidation on a close below about $523.
  • $XMTR (momentum): Digital-manufacturing marketplace with relative strength of 95 and Q2 revenue up 41%. Levels: pivot about $113 (record high), support about $107, invalidation about $96.50.
  • $MPC (momentum, repeat): Refining margins near records, the refiner group moving together, and Barclays raised its target to $488 on Monday. Levels: pivot $470, support about $455, invalidation on a close below $440.
  • $TSLA (social): Reddit and StockTwits buzz on the Q3 deliveries beat and a reported school-zone robotaxi probe; a repair chart below its 200-day near $392, with earnings Wed Oct 21 after the close. Levels: watch $400, support about $371, invalidation on a close below about $348.
  • $CON (sleeper): Largest US occupational-health provider, making orderly new 52-week highs after raising guidance. Levels: pivot about $36.80, support about $34.70 (50-day), invalidation on a close below about $34.25.

---

notes_html:
Week of October 5th, 2026. $MPC $MTRN $TWLO $NVDA $CHEF

The (Stock) Watchlist is back for the first time since summer 2020: three momentum leaders, one social-buzz name and one under-the-radar sleeper for the week of Oct 5. Data as of the Fri Oct 2 close (MPC prices as of the Thu Oct 1 close).

Market pulse

  • September payrolls rose just 29K, cutting October Fed hike odds from about 64% to about 20%. The Nasdaq 100 closed at a record, but the S&P 500 (-0.3%) and Dow (-1.3%) fell on the week as the 10-year yield closed at 5.28% after hitting its highest levels since 2002 this week.
  • Breadth is narrow: only about a quarter of S&P 500 stocks are above their 50-day. Brent is still above $100 on the Iran war. Takeaway: be picky, leadership is narrow.
  • Week ahead: FOMC minutes and a $39B 10-year note auction (Wed Oct 7), PepsiCo (Thu), Delta (Fri). Weekend: Yemen's Houthis claimed an attack on an Aramco facility in Riyadh; damage unconfirmed.

The picks

  • $MPC: Momentum leader. Refiner that logged six straight weekly gains in September on a record diesel crack, then jumped about 6% Thursday to about $420 on fuel-shortage headlines, a couple percent under its all-time high (reportedly about $431). Friday's G7 diesel reserve release is the twist. Levels: breakout on a close above about $431, support $400, setup breaks below $380.
  • $MTRN: Momentum leader. Beryllium and advanced-materials maker with a record Q2 and two guidance raises this year; closed about $312 Friday after an intraday all-time high near $314. No company news found to explain Friday's pop. Stretched (roughly 25% above its 50-day) and rich (about 45x guided earnings). Levels: trigger on a close above $314, support $290, breaks below $285.
  • $TWLO: Momentum leader. Joins the S&P 500 before Tuesday's open; index buying normally lands in Monday's closing auction. Closed about $301, just under its $306 52-week high (not an all-time high). Roughly 30% above its 50-day, so this one is about the reaction, not a chase. Levels: close above $306 once it's in the index, support $290, breaks below $280.
  • $NVDA: Social buzz. First record since May (about $238 intraday, closed about $234), a fresh breakout attempt only about 7% above a rising 50-day. Record $150B buyback addition; Morgan Stanley restored it as its top chip pick. Retail returning, not stampeding: Stocktwits called chatter normal and sentiment neutral. Levels: confirmation on a close above about $238, support and line in the sand at the rising 50-day near $218, 200-day near $207 below that.
  • $CHEF: Under-the-radar sleeper. About $4.8B specialty food distributor to fine-dining restaurants and hotels; new all-time high Friday out of a month-long range, only about 7% above a rising 50-day. Not cheap at about 47x earnings, and Q3 results are not yet scheduled. Levels: trigger on a close above about $118.50 on rising volume, support near $110, breaks below $105.

Scorecard: None yet. Starting next week, every pick is logged and graded against the S&P 500.
